description: WinDivert (Windows Packet Divert): signed kernel driver and library for capturing, filtering, changing and re-injecting network packets from user mode. The driver under zapret, zapret2 and zapret-discord-youtube (and GoodbyeDPI). Includes windivertctl and the sample tools.
notes: Global install only, from an elevated (admin) shell: scoop install -g gesu/WinDivert
Programs load the driver from the folder of their WinDivert.dll; it stays loaded until a reboot or windivertctl uninstall.
gesu/zapret, gesu/zapret2 and gesu/zapret-discord-youtube get copies of WinDivert.dll and WinDivert64.sys
from this package each time it is installed or updated (while their winws is not running).
Command: windivertctl list | watch | kill [filter] | uninstall (admin). Scoop Apps: 'WinDivert' shows them.
The samples (netdump, netfilter, passthru, socketdump, streamdump, flowtrack, webfilter) are in
Antivirus programs often flag WinDivert as a risk tool (Not-a-virus:RiskTool.WinDivert). The driver is
signed and the files are upstream's own; add an exclusion if yours quarantines them.
pre_install: if (!$global) { error "$app puts a driver or a service on the system, which runs as SYSTEM: install it globally, so that only administrators can change its files: scoop install -g gesu/$app"; break }

if ([System.Runtime.InteropServices.RuntimeInformation]::OSArchitecture -eq 'Arm64') { error "$app has no ARM64 build: the WinDivert driver is x64 only (ARM64 Windows would need test signing)."; break }
# One set of files in the app folder: x86 has WinDivert32.sys for 32-bit Windows and WinDivert64.sys for
# The 'WinDivert' shortcut opens this micro-launcher: windivertctl.exe without arguments only prints its usage.

post_install: # Copy the new files to the zapret packages that use them (scripts/zapret/Sync-ZapretComponents.ps1).
# A copy fails while that package's winws runs; 'zapret-discord-youtube sync' or 'scoop update -f' redo it.
pre_uninstall: # A driver service registered from this app's folder (by windivertctl or the samples here) would keep
# pointing at deleted files: stop it, and on uninstall remove it. Services of other folders stay.
if ($cmd -eq 'uninstall') { sc.exe delete $name | Out-Null; info "Removed the '$name' driver service." }
